provenance.note: Generated by drivers/regression on the pystatsval harness against a PyPI-installed pystatistics==3.18.0. Correctness fits both pystatistics and the R reference on the identical design; scaling sweeps synthetic designs per device. Two hosts: powerhouse (Apple Silicon, CPU fp64 + Metal/MPS fp32, R 4.5.2) and forge (NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti, CPU fp64 + CUDA fp32, R 4.3.3).

reference.name: R stats::lm / stats::glm / MASS::glm.nb
reference.what: R's lm() (OLS via pivoted QR) and glm() (GLM via IRLS), plus MASS::glm.nb() for the negative binomial. Because pystatistics unifies lm and glm, the head-to-head pulls from both.

studies.title: Correctness vs R — Powerhouse (Apple Silicon, CPU / fp64)
Correctness vs R — Forge (Linux x86-64, CPU / fp64)
Device scaling — Powerhouse: CPU (fp64) vs MPS (fp32)
studies.note: GLM (binomial) accelerator cells are blank on MPS: the GPU IRLS inner solve uses torch.linalg.lstsq, which is unsupported on the Metal backend, so every GLM-MPS fit errors and no accelerator time is recorded. Only OLS scales on MPS here; CUDA (Forge) carries the GLM-on-GPU story.

record_fields.coef_max_rel: max relative difference between pystatistics and R over the coefficient vector (correctness headline)
record_fields.se_max_rel: max relative difference over the standard-error vector
record_fields.tstat_max_rel: max relative difference over the t/z-statistic vector
record_fields.pval_max_abs: max absolute difference over the p-value vector
record_fields.speedup_vs_r: R wall-clock / pystatistics wall-clock on the same fit (>1 means pystatistics is faster)
record_fields.wall_median_s: median wall-clock over timed repeats (headline timing statistic)
record_fields.peak_mem_mb: peak memory during the fit (GPU allocator high-water mark on device; process RSS delta on CPU)
